# Gate topology

<!-- Generated by tools/gatetool from test/gates/gates.yaml. Do not edit by hand; run `make gates-write`. -->

Every verification command this repository runs, the question it actually
answers, and the shipped surfaces it drives.

A gate reports on what it drives and nothing else. Reading a green gate as
a broader claim than the `Answers` column makes is the specific mistake
this table exists to prevent: the conformance suite has been green while a
defect lived in three shipped sign-in paths it never routes through.

**Levels.** `static` reads or compiles a surface without executing it.
`unit` runs it in-process. `integration` drives it as a deployed
artifact — a booted example, a real browser, a real storage backend, or the
external conformance suite. A surface reached only at `static` level is
one nothing ever runs.

## Gates

| Gate | Make target | In `make verify` | Level | Answers |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gofmt` | — | yes | static | Whether every Go file already matches gofumpt and goimports output. |
| `vet` | `make vet` | yes | static | Whether go vet's analyzers flag a construct in any module of the tree. |
| `lint` | `make lint` | yes | static | Whether golangci-lint's configured analyzer set flags the tree, including the depguard and forbidigo rules that enforce this project's own bans. |
| `test` | `make test` | no | unit | Whether the in-process test suite passes against the in-memory reference store. |
| `test-race` | `make test-race` | yes | unit | Whether the in-process suite passes with the race detector armed. |
| `tool-tests` | — | yes | unit | Whether the gate tools' own suites pass. Their modules sit outside the shipping inventory, so `make test` never reaches them and `scripts/verify.sh` runs them as a separate step. |
| `fuzz` | `make fuzz` | no | unit | Whether the registered fuzz targets find a crashing input within the time budget. |
| `govulncheck` | `make govulncheck` | no | static | Whether any reachable dependency symbol appears in the Go vulnerability database. |
| `licenses` | `make licenses` | no | static | Whether every dependency's license is on the allowed list. |
| `scenario-validate` | `make scenario-validate` | yes | static | Whether every catalog file conforms to the catalog schema. |
| `scenario-coverage` | `make scenario-coverage-strict` | yes | static | Whether every in-scope catalog row is bound to a test that exists and runs. |
| `scenario-shape` | `make scenario-shape` | yes | static | Whether each catalog feature file states enough about values, ordering and identity rather than only about presence. |
| `scenario-advisories` | `make scenario-advisories-strict` | yes | static | Whether every catalogued CVE/GHSA has a `// Tracks:` annotation and every annotation names a catalogued advisory. |
| `stability` | `make stability-check` | yes | static | Whether the recorded per-symbol stability markers still match the godoc, and whether a release rewrites a row already recorded. |
| `reach` | `make reach` | yes | static | Whether every exported constant, Err-prefixed sentinel, catalogued audit event, seed message key and DynamoDB index is both named in non-test library code and branched on outside its own enumeration plumbing. |
| `doc-refs` | — | yes | static | Whether documentation cross-references resolve to files that exist. |
| `version-refs` | — | yes | static | Whether the version strings quoted across README, examples and manifests agree. |
| `gates` | `make gates` | yes | static | Whether the declared gate topology still matches the tree — surfaces resolve, script-running Makefile targets are accounted for, and no surface is left with nothing that runs it. |
| `failopen` | `make failopen` | yes | static | Whether any branch turns a storage read's error into a fabricated negative without carrying the error anywhere. |
| `verify-examples` | `make verify-examples` | yes | static | Whether every example compiles and vets, and whether the static documentation checks over the examples pass. |
| `apiverify` | `make verify-examples-api` | no | integration | Whether each non-browser example boots as a real process and does what its header doc promises, driven over HTTP with a real cookie jar. |
| `browserverify` | `make verify-examples-browser` | no | integration | Whether the browser-driven examples and the reference application complete a real sign-in in Chrome. |
| `store-contracts` | — | no | integration | Whether each storage adapter satisfies the shared store contract against a real engine started in a container. |
| `conformance` | `make conformance-release-verify` | no | integration | Whether the candidate OFCS run has the reference module catalog and every module passed, matched an exclusion entry, or fell under an accepted-outcome rule. |

## What each gate cannot see

A green result from the gate on the left says nothing about the classes on the right.

**`gofmt`**

- Anything about what the code does. Formatting is orthogonal to behaviour.

**`vet`**

- Logic that is well-formed but wrong. vet has no model of this project's invariants.
- Code behind a build tag the run does not select.

**`lint`**

- A rule nobody wrote. The banned-construct set is exactly what .golangci.yml enumerates.
- A violation inside a directory the config excludes.

**`test`**

- Behaviour no test asserts. Coverage of the catalog is a separate gate, and the catalog's own completeness is not measured by either.
- Data races, which need the -race variant.
- Anything that only appears against a real storage engine or a real browser.

**`test-race`**

- A race on a path no test drives concurrently. The detector reports interleavings that happen, not those that could.
- Everything the plain unit gate is blind to.

**`tool-tests`**

- Whether a gate's predicate is the right one. A tool can be correct about the wrong question, which is how the reach gate shipped a weaker predicate than its description claimed.

**`fuzz`**

- Any parser with no fuzz target registered against it.
- Semantic errors. A fuzz target reports crashes and failed assertions, not wrong answers.

**`govulncheck`**

- A vulnerability with no advisory yet.
- A defect in this repository's own code.

**`licenses`**

- License terms a scanner classifies but misreads.
- Anything about code correctness.

**`scenario-validate`**

- A requirement no row states. A missing row is not a schema violation.

**`scenario-coverage`**

- Completeness of the catalog itself. 100% measures fidelity to the rows that were written, not that the right rows were written.
- A row that asserts a claim is present without asserting its value. The shape gate reports that ratio; this gate counts such a row as covered.

**`scenario-shape`**

- Whether a value-shaped row asserts the right value. The gate reads the declared shape, not the assertion.
- A feature with no catalog file at all.

**`scenario-advisories`**

- A vulnerability class with no advisory. Most defects this project finds are not published advisories.

**`stability`**

- Whether a symbol marked stable behaves as its previous release did. The gate reads markers, not behaviour.

**`reach`**

- Whether the branch it finds is the right one. A constant consulted by a wrong comparison passes.
- A value reached only through a string literal rather than the constant. The check follows identifiers, so an internal package spelling the same wire value by hand looks like nothing consulting the constant.
- Behaviour of the code that does name the symbol.

**`doc-refs`**

- Whether the prose at the other end still says what the reference claims.

**`version-refs`**

- Whether the quoted version is the right one to ship.

**`gates`**

- Whether a gate's `answers` line is honest. The map records claims; only a reader checks them.
- Whether a gate that claims a surface exercises it well.

**`failopen`**

- A fail-open written in a shape the pattern does not match — an error assigned to an outer variable and then dropped, or a negative produced two calls later.
- Whether the distinction the branch does draw is drawn correctly.
- A store method whose name is outside the read set the check recognises.

**`verify-examples`**

- Any configuration the library now rejects at construction. Nothing here calls op.New, so an example that can no longer start compiles green.

**`apiverify`**

- Rendering, framing defenses and anything else that needs a browser.
- The docker-compose examples, which it does not start.

**`browserverify`**

- Everything, when Chrome is absent — the harness skips unless BROWSERVERIFY_REQUIRED is set.
- Browsers other than the one installed.

**`store-contracts`**

- Engine versions other than the pinned images.
- Contract clauses the generated suite does not cover.

**`conformance`**

- Any flow the suite does not route through. It drives one authenticated session per plan and never follows an add-account link, so multi-account behaviour is entirely outside it.
- Anything an embedder does. The suite exercises op-demo's configuration, not every configuration the library allows.
